the N1/MMN; P3a; RON chain is not a strongly coupled chain.
the processes indexed at the three stages of distraction are not strongly coupled and that the processes indexed as P3a and the RON are dissociable.
P3a, MMN, and RON do not reflect the three processing stages of distraction, as assumed in previous studies.

the temporal dynamics of distraction and provides new insights into the mechanisms underlying the three processing stages of distraction.
the functional architecture of the brain network underlying auditory distraction.
the functional role and the neural correlates of the P3a and the RON.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the processes indexed are not strongly coupled but are at least partially independent.
P3a and N1/MMN are not strongly coupled, and that P3a is not strongly coupled with RON, but that RON is strongly coupled with N1/MMN.
the processes indexed at each stage are not strongly coupled, although they are related to each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three ERPs reflect different processes that are not strongly coupled, and thus, the three ERPs should not necessarily be interpreted in a serial model of distraction.
P3a is not necessarily preceded by N1-increase, MMN elicitation, or RON elicitation.
the three ERPs are not part of a strongly coupled chain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the three ERPs reflecting the stages of distraction do not form a strongly coupled sequence.
the processes indexed at the three stages of distraction may be dissociated from each other.
the processes indexed in a distraction paradigm are not strictly ordered, but rather form a loose chain.
